YOUR WORKFLOW

From source to editable slides

  1. Bring your source

    Upload a PDF with selectable text, Word (.docx), TXT, or Markdown (.md), up to 10 MB. If you have only a topic, start with an AI draft.

  2. Check the text

    Read the extracted text or draft. Correct names and figures, and check that headings and important sections are present before you generate.

  3. Choose a visual direction

    Pick a theme, template, and spacing that fit the material. Add photos or a logo where they support the story.

  4. Generate the deck

    Start generation from the reviewed material. If the draft is missing an important point, update the source first so it has the context it needs.

  5. Review slide by slide

    Check the layout and source coverage. Pay particular attention to figures, dates, and conclusions before sharing.

  6. Export and refine

    Download the editable PowerPoint when the export is ready. Open it in PowerPoint to make final edits before presenting.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Troubleshoot your presentation

Why is my PDF empty after import?

A scanned PDF may contain images without selectable text. Run OCR first, or paste the text into a TXT, Markdown, or Word document and upload that file.

What if my document is too large or too long?

Keep the upload under 10 MB. If the extracted text is too long, split it by topic or use the sections relevant to this deck.

Can I make a presentation without a document?

Yes. Start from a topic and review the AI draft before generating. Add any facts, figures, or wording the deck needs to retain.

What if a slide misses an important point?

Compare the deck with the reviewed source. Make the missing point explicit in the source or draft, then generate again if you need a revised deck.

Can I edit the exported slides?

Yes. Download the .pptx after the export is ready and open it in PowerPoint to edit the slide elements.
